Use the universal property of the quotient by the ring congruence \(c\).

- The assumption \(H : c \le \ker f\) says exactly that \(f\) is constant on \(c\)-equivalence classes, so it induces the well-defined homomorphism
  \[
  \operatorname{lift}(f,H) : M/c \to P.
  \]
- First establish its computation rule on representatives:
  \[
  \operatorname{lift}(f,H)([x])=f(x).
  \]
  By extensionality of ring homomorphisms, this immediately gives
  \[
  \operatorname{lift}(f,H)\circ \operatorname{mk}'=f,
  \]
  proving the second conjunct.
- For uniqueness, suppose \(g\circ\operatorname{mk}'=f\). Every element of \(M/c\) has a representative \([x]\); on such an element, the hypothesis and the computation rule show
  \[
  g([x])=f(x)=\operatorname{lift}(f,H)([x]).
  \]
  Quotient induction, or equivalently extensionality using the surjectivity of \(\operatorname{mk}'\), then yields \(g=\operatorname{lift}(f,H)\).

The essential mechanism is therefore existence and uniqueness in the quotient’s universal property; \(H\) is precisely the well-definedness condition.
